question.leadin: Answer the following about German invasions during World War II.
question.text: Germany invaded this country and Denmark as part of Operation Weserubung. This country was home to German heavy water production and was led by Vidkun Quisling after its surrender.
question.clue: In 1905, it elected Prince Carl as its king, breaking up a union that had been forced since the Treaty of Kiel.

swap.leadin: The continent of Europe is home to many notable seas of the world.
swap.text: This sea in eastern Europe names the region containing Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia. Stockholm, Sweden, lies on the shores of this sea.
swap.clue: The defeat of Wendish tribes along this body's southern shores led to the rise of the Viking Age, and the modern Kaliningrad Oblast borders this body.

question.leadin: The author of the Prose Edda, Snorri Sturluson, was a law speaker of a parliament in this country.
question.text: Name this country home to the Althing, so-named to trick people to move to Greenland.
question.clue: The ruling chiefs of this country established the Althing in the early 900s, one of the oldest continuously meeting parliaments in the world.

swap.text: Viking expansion beyond Scandinavia included the founding of a permanent colony on Greenland by this father of Leif Erikson.
swap.clue: During that exile, he established an estate at Brattahlith.

question.leadin: This country formed a dual monarchy with Denmark after the collapse of the Kalmar Union in 1521.
question.text: Name this country whose kings include Harald Hardrada.
question.clue: This country ruled two areas later annexed by the Kingdom of Alba and Scotland; those were, respectively, the Hebrides and Orkney.

swap.text: After Gustavus Adolphus died, this advisor of his took charge and continued to lead Swedish forces. He would go on to serve as advisor to Gustavus Adolphus' daughter and successor, Cristina.
swap.clue: This man corresponded extensively with the Dutch merchant Samuel Blommaert ("BLOM-art") to set up a New World colony with his country's "South Company."

question.leadin: This leader was killed instantly by a shot to the head during the Siege of Fredriksten.
question.text: Name this monarch who ruled Sweden from 1697 to 1718.
question.answerHtml: Charles XII of Sweden [accept Carl XII; accept Carolus Rex]
question.clue: In one campaign, this man installed Stanis? aw Leszczy?

swap.leadin: This country once formed a dual monarchy with Norway.
swap.text: Name this Scandinavian nation that was led by Christian X in the early twentieth century.
swap.clue: It's not Norway, but English kings Harold Harefoot and Harthacanute were from this country.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Age of Liberty.
question.text: The Age of Liberty began after this war, after which the Swedish king fled to the Ottoman Empire following a failed military alliance with the Cossacks.
question.clue: During this war, one side relieved a siege during a snowstorm at the Battle of Narva.

swap.leadin: It arose over the control of the Hanko naval base and was prosecuted by the coalition government of Risto Ryti.
swap.text: Name this war which saw the use of the Mannerheim line in an attempt to repel a Soviet invasion.
swap.clue: One sniper in this war had 505 confirmed kills, earning him the nickname "White Death".

question.text: Until 1597, most of Tycho's observations were undertaken at this observatory, devoted to his Muse, on the Isle of Hven. It notably lacked a telescope.

swap.text: This Norwegian claim, located between the British and Australian claims at 20 degrees West and around 44 degrees East, was named by Roald Amundsen after the wife of King Haakon VII.
swap.clue: The Prime Meridian also passes through this Antarctic region. Claimed by Norway, this region is named for the wife of King Haakon VII ["the seventh"], who reigned from 1905 to 1957, and who was also the daughter of King Edward VII ["the seventh"] of Great Britain.

question.leadin: Answer the following about emigration from the Eastern Bloc.
question.text: A series of 1975 accords signed in this country's capital eased Eastern Bloc immigration policies during a detente in US-Soviet relations. This country continued a policy of "active neutrality" under Urho Kekkonen.
question.answerHtml: Finland [or Suomi; or Republic of Finland or Suomen tasavalta or Republiken Finland] (The accords were the Helsinki Accords.)
question.clue: Frederick Charles of Hesse was the only king of this country, which produced a soldier nicknamed "White Death" for being the deadliest sniper in history.

swap.text: The Kalmar Union was founded by this monarch, who ordered that the False Olaf be burned with a necklace of his forged letters as kindling. The Victual Brothers were employed against this "Semiramis of the North" during her siege of Stockholm.
swap.answerHtml: Margaret I of Denmark [accept Margaret Valdemarsdotter; prompt on Margaret]
swap.clue: This ruler, who was often mocked as being "Pantsless" by Albert of Mecklenburg, was the first target of the Victual Brothers, who provided supplies to counteract this ruler's siege of Stockholm.

question.text: Born with the name Boguslaw, this adoptive son of Margaret I adopted a more Nordic-sounding regnal name when she put him on the throne of the Kalmar Union. He later introduced the Sound Dues.
question.answerHtml: Eric of Pomerania [or Erik af Pommern, Eric VII, Eric III, or Eric XIII; prompt on Eric]

swap.text: A Danish king of this name, the third from the House of Glucksburg and tenth overall, gave a curt reply to Hitler's birthday telegram, which prompted the "Telegram crisis." That king of this name dismissed his government at the end of the Easter Crisis.
swap.clue: In addition to Vilhelm Buhl, another prime minister who served under this king was deposed after failing to call a referendum regarding the return of Flensburg to his country, and that prime minister was named Carl Theodor Zahle.

question.leadin: This erector of the Jelling Stones was the first Danish king to be baptized.
question.text: Name this unifier of Denmark, the son of Gorm the Old.

swap.text: Admiral Jellicoe's greatest triumph came at this May 31, 1916, naval engagement that saw the defeat of the German fleet under Reinhard Scheer.
swap.clue: The Battle of Dybbol in the Second Schleswig War took place in this region which makes up most of modern-day Denmark. John Jellicoe led British forces at an inconclusive World War I naval battle named for this body of land.

question.leadin: He had to deal with revolts in Dalarna and one led by Nils Dacke, and at the Diet of Vasteras, he confiscated the property of Sweden's Catholic Church.
question.text: Name this founder of the Vasa dynasty who signed the Treaty of Malmo with Christian II, thus relieving Sweden of Denmark's rule in the Kalmar Union.

swap.text: After losing at Poltava, Charles fled to this Turkish fortress in modern day Moldova. Eventually, the Ottomans tired of Charles and sent in the military to arrest him. During the ensuing skirmish at this place, Axel Erik Roos reportedly saved the king's life three times, and Charles was only stopped after he tripped on his own spurs.
swap.clue: During a "kalabalik" at this location, Axel Erik Roos saved his employer's life three times.
